requirements.title: Executable constructs containing blocks are a closed construct set
requirements.definition: The executable constructs that contain blocks are the listed ASSOCIATE, BLOCK, CHANGE TEAM, CRITICAL, DO, IF, SELECT CASE, SELECT RANK, and SELECT TYPE constructs. This is a classification of construct families; each construct owns its own syntax and execution rules.

pending.listed-block-construct-families: PENDING source-control inventory check using one admitted form from each listed construct family after that family is registered; this facet records classification only and does not claim execution behavior for unregistered 11.1.5+ constructs.

requirements.oracle: Classification evidence only; no diagnostic is attributed to p1 for a construct not being on the list.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This source-only catalogue records pending plans only. It creates no Fortran test program, invokes no processor, approves no fixture or oracle, and claims no coverage. Future fixtures must use independently derived literal values, inquiry results, or source relationships; must ensure discriminating non-vacuous observations for association, scope, bounds, and control-flow claims; must not infer statement execution counts, evaluation order beyond the cited rule, side effects, temporary storage, image ordering, addresses, descriptor layout, or processor-dependent representations; and must not rely on compiler agreement, message wording, emitted code, undefined values, resource exhaustion, or a processor-dependent value.

requirements.title: A block is a possibly empty sequence of execution-part constructs
requirements.definition: The grammar production for block is zero or more execution-part-constructs. Empty-block admission and the contents of execution-part-construct are owned by the construct using the block and by the execution-part grammar.

pending.empty-block-form: PENDING positive-control source forms with an empty block in constructs that permit one, such as an empty BLOCK construct after local syntax constraints are satisfied.

requirements.title: Executable constructs control block execution and bound their blocks by construct-specific statements
requirements.definition: Executable constructs are the language mechanism for controlling which blocks execute or how many times a block executes. Blocks are bounded by statements particular to the construct in which they are embedded; the actual selection, iteration, synchronization, or termination behavior is owned by each construct subclause.
